title: Userland Structural Assumptions — Galactic Cherry Marvell Edition 98
author: MEARVK LLC
purpose: Document the structural assumptions, threading models, message-passing norms, security concerns, and normality expectations for every userland component. Companion to kernel-structure.json and executable-formats-sketch.json.
base_userland: Ubuntu Base 24.04.4 LTS (US Treasury & MEARVK LLC) — ubuntu-base-24.04.4-base-amd64.tar.gz
architecture: x86_64 — x86-64-v3 baseline (AVX2, FMA, BMI2, POPCNT)

jdesk.purpose: Cross-platform JavaFX desktop environment. Full-screen white-theme window manager, taskbar, icon grid, and native application launcher.
jdesk.status: Active — libjdesk.so built, icons/manifests deployed to /opt/jdesk/

key_classes: JDeskApplication (entry point — not yet written, pending)
javafx_layer.threading_model: JavaFX Application Thread for all UI. Monitor threads are daemon threads (one per launched app). NativeBridge calls are synchronous blocking from FX thread.
javafx_layer.message_passing: JavaFX property/event system. NativeAppLauncher communicates with processes via ProcessBuilder — no IPC bus. Process exit detected by Thread.waitFor() in daemon monitor thread.

native_layer.cpu_features_detected: SSE2/3/4.1/4.2, AVX, AVX2, AVX-512F/BW, FMA, AES-NI, POPCNT, RDTSC, BMI1/2, RDRAND

threading_concerns.xlib_thread_safety: XInitThreads() must be called before any other Xlib call — enforced in jdesk_init()
threading_concerns.jni_callback_thread: Event callbacks from native fire on a non-FX thread — must Platform.runLater() before touching scene graph
threading_concerns.vsync_blocking: jdesk_vsync_wait() is a blocking call — must not run on FX thread

manifest_layer.format: Java Properties (.jdesk-app) — name, binary, args, icon, profile, desktop, panel, resource overrides
manifest_layer.memory_proxy_profile: jdesk-apps.xml — 9 profiles (writer, ide, browser, terminal, files, settings, windows-app, macos-app, kali-security)

native_apps.provisioner: jdesk-provision (bash, 20K) — installs Linux ELF natives at first boot
native_apps.kali_provisioner: kali-provision (bash, 20K) — installs 25 pentest tools within 250MB budget

security_concerns.SEC_JD_001: libjdesk.so loaded via System.loadLibrary — path must be /usr/local/lib, not world-writable
security_concerns.SEC_JD_002: NativeAppLauncher.launch() exec()s binaries by path — path must be validated to prevent injection
security_concerns.SEC_JD_003: .jdesk-app manifest files in /opt/jdesk/manifests/ must be owned by root or mearvk — not world-writable
security_concerns.SEC_JD_004: kali-provision installs pentest tools — must not be run as root except for apt installs
security_concerns.SEC_JD_005: Chromium launched with --no-sandbox — acceptable only in sandboxed desktop session, not server
security_concerns.SEC_JD_006: Memory Proxy profile (jdesk-apps.xml) — RAM/thread limits enforced by JVM, not kernel — can be bypassed by native code

normality_concerns.desktop_startup_time: < 3 seconds from JVM start to icon grid visible
normality_concerns.app_launch_time: < 500ms from double-click to process start (ELF); + 2-5s Wine overhead (PE); + 3-8s Darling (Mach-O)
normality_concerns.memory_per_icon_cell: < 1MB per rendered cell in scene graph
normality_concerns.concern: More than 6 running apps simultaneously will pressure RAM budget — writer+ide+browser alone = ~2GB soft limit

java_web_server.purpose: NitroWebExpress (NWE) — full Java web application server with telnet TUI, REST API, and web interface. Primary MEARVK application server.
java_web_server.size_on_disk: 587 MB (includes compiled JARs, Tomcat, MySQL connector, module output)

stack.gateway: NWE Gateway — NAT traversal, auto-start service

threading_model.main_thread: Tomcat acceptor — accepts connections on port 8080
threading_model.worker_threads: Tomcat thread pool (NIO connector) — default 200 threads max
threading_model.module_threads: Each NWE module may spawn its own executor

concerns.THR_NWE_001: Thread pool exhaustion under load — monitor active vs max threads via JMX
concerns.THR_NWE_002: Module threads must not share static mutable state without synchronization
concerns.THR_NWE_003: Telnet sessions run as the invoking user grade — enforce per-session privilege limits

message_passing.client_to_server: HTTP/1.1 + HTTPS (Apache → Tomcat via AJP or reverse proxy)
message_passing.telnet_protocol: Line-oriented TUI over raw TCP port 23 — commands dispatched to module handlers
message_passing.module_ipc: In-process method calls — modules loaded via classloader into same JVM
message_passing.database: JDBC over Unix socket (localhost MySQL) — connection pool (HikariCP or Tomcat JDBC)

security_concerns.SEC_NWE_001: Telnet (port 23) is plaintext — acceptable only on localhost or VPN, never public internet
security_concerns.SEC_NWE_002: Module classloader isolation — modules share JVM heap, malicious module can access other modules' memory
security_concerns.SEC_NWE_003: MySQL credentials must not be in source — use /etc/nwe/db.properties (mode 600, owned root)
security_concerns.SEC_NWE_004: Apache AJP connector (port 8009) — Ghostcat (CVE-2020-1938) mitigated by disabling or requiring secret
security_concerns.SEC_NWE_005: Tomcat default session timeout — should be ≤ 30 minutes for authenticated sessions
security_concerns.SEC_NWE_006: nwe.jar is 27.5MB — contains compiled bytecode trivially decompilable; do not embed secrets
security_concerns.SEC_NWE_007: Gateway NAT traversal — ensure outbound connections are to expected endpoints only

normality_concerns.startup_time: < 30 seconds from java invocation to HTTP 200 on port 8080
normality_concerns.gc_pause_frequency: < 1 GC pause per second under normal load
normality_concerns.concern: Heap growth above 3GB indicates memory leak in a module — check classloader leaks

x11.purpose: X.Org display server and client libraries — provides the display substrate for JDesk. Built from source tarballs.
x11.status: Source present — built output in x11/_build/

threading_model.xserver: Single-threaded event dispatch loop with per-client I/O threads
threading_model.xcb_clients: Fully async — requests queued, replies via xcb_wait_for_reply()
threading_model.xlib_clients: Synchronous by default — XSync()/XFlush() required for ordering
threading_model.jdesk_usage: libjdesk.so uses Xlib with XInitThreads() — safe for multi-threaded JVM

message_passing.event_model: Server pushes events to client event queue — client polls with XNextEvent()/xcb_poll_for_event()
message_passing.clipboard: X11 selection mechanism — CLIPBOARD, PRIMARY, SECONDARY atoms

security_concerns.SEC_X11_001: X11 has no authentication by default beyond xauth cookies — DISPLAY=:0 socket is accessible to all processes of the user
security_concerns.SEC_X11_002: X11 screen capture trivial — any client can call XGetImage() on root window — full desktop screenshot without permission
security_concerns.SEC_X11_003: X11 keylogging trivial — XGrabKeyboard() or XQueryKeymap() gives any client access to keystrokes
security_concerns.SEC_X11_004: XAUTHORITY file must be mode 600 — leaking it allows remote X connections
security_concerns.SEC_X11_005: libX11 server extension negotiation — extensions loaded from /usr/lib/xorg/modules/ must be signed or verified
security_concerns.known_gap: X11 was designed for trusted local networks — no process isolation between X clients sharing a display

normality_concerns.x_connection_startup: < 100ms to open Display and get screen geometry
normality_concerns.render_throughput: XRender compositing — 60fps at 1920x1080 typical on modern GPU
normality_concerns.concern: DISPLAY=:0 not set or X server not running will cause jdesk_display_open() to return NULL — JDesk startup will fail silently without null check

openjdk.purpose: MEARVK custom OpenJDK 28 build with jvm-config.xml extensions, jvmMemoryProxy, and class-load guard.
openjdk.status: Source patches present — requires JDK 28 EA build to compile

jvmMemoryProxy.purpose: Per-application resource governance — RAM soft/hard limits, disk I/O rate, thread count, CPU window. Enforced via -memory-guard JVM flag.

threading_concerns.THR_JMP_001: Memory proxy monitors run on JVM housekeeping threads — must not block application threads
threading_concerns.THR_JMP_002: Disk I/O rate limiting uses token bucket — bucket state is shared across threads, needs atomic ops
threading_concerns.THR_JMP_003: Hard RAM limit triggers OOM kill of the governed process — must flush pending I/O first

jvm_config_xml.purpose: Declarative JVM flag configuration — replaces command-line -XX flags with versioned XML

class_load_guard.purpose: Enforce per-grade limits on how many application classes can be loaded — prevents runaway plugin classloading

openjdk.boot_jdk: userland/java/boot-jdk-27/ (required to compile JDK 28 from source)

security_concerns.SEC_JDK_001: jvm-config.xml must not be world-writable — an attacker could raise heap limits or disable class-load-guard
security_concerns.SEC_JDK_002: observer_circuit SSH port 2222 — must require key-based auth, no password auth
security_concerns.SEC_JDK_003: mysql_bridge credentials — must use least-privilege MySQL user (SELECT only on jvm_operand)
security_concerns.SEC_JDK_004: HeapDumpPath /var/log/jvm — heap dumps contain all in-memory data including passwords and keys; mode 700
security_concerns.SEC_JDK_005: jvmMemoryProxy hard limits — a process that exceeds RAM hard limit is killed; ensure graceful shutdown hooks run first
security_concerns.SEC_JDK_006: Class-load guard bypass — native agents (JVMTI) can load classes bypassing the guard; agents must be vetted

normality_concerns.jvm_startup_time: < 2 seconds to first bytecode for server JVM with G1GC
normality_concerns.class_load_time: < 5000 classes for typical NWE module startup
normality_concerns.gc_overhead: < 5% of wall time in GC under normal load
normality_concerns.metaspace_growth: Metaspace stable after warmup — growth after stabilization indicates classloader leak
normality_concerns.concern: JDK 28 EA is pre-release — production deployments should pin to a specific EA build tag

wine.purpose: Win32/Win64 API translation layer — enables execution of Windows PE binaries on Linux under JDesk Memory Proxy governance.
wine.status: Source present — requires ./configure && make to build

architecture.wineserver: Daemon process that implements Windows kernel services (registry, synchronization objects, process/thread management)
architecture.ntdll.dll.so: Windows NT layer — maps Windows syscalls to Linux syscalls
architecture.user32.dll.so: Win32 window management — translated to X11 via Xlib
architecture.gdi32.dll.so: Graphics Device Interface — rendered via X11/XRender
architecture.loader: wine64 / wine — PE loader, sets up process address space

threading_model.model: Each Windows thread maps to a Linux thread. wineserver is single-threaded with select() event loop.

concerns.THR_WINE_001: wineserver is a single point of contention — all synchronization objects (mutexes, events, semaphores) go through it
concerns.THR_WINE_002: Windows TLS (Thread Local Storage) implemented via pthread keys — max 64 keys per process
concerns.THR_WINE_003: Windows fibers (cooperative coroutines) implemented with setjmp/longjmp — stack switching not signal-safe

message_passing.windows_messages: WM_* messages dispatched via wineserver message queue — translated by user32.dll.so
message_passing.ipc_to_linux: Windows named pipes mapped to Unix FIFOs; mailslots emulated in wineserver
message_passing.dde: Dynamic Data Exchange — legacy, emulated via wineserver

memory_model.base_overhead: ~200MB RAM for wineserver + core DLLs on first launch
memory_model.per_app_overhead: Windows process address space starts at 0x400000 (32-bit) or 0x140000000 (64-bit)
memory_model.memory_proxy_wrap: libjdesk.so wraps wine invocation: java -memory-guard -Xguard:profile=windows-app wine <binary>

security_concerns.SEC_WINE_001: Wine does NOT sandbox the Windows application — a malicious .exe has full access to the Linux filesystem via Wine's drive_c mapping
security_concerns.SEC_WINE_002: wine drive_c maps to ~/.wine/drive_c by default — symlink attacks can escape to host filesystem
security_concerns.SEC_WINE_003: Windows DLL injection techniques work in Wine — a malicious PE can load arbitrary DLLs
security_concerns.SEC_WINE_004: WINEPREFIX isolation — each application should use a separate WINEPREFIX to limit cross-app interference
security_concerns.SEC_WINE_005: wineserver socket in /tmp/.wine-<uid>/ — must be mode 700 to prevent other users connecting to it
security_concerns.known_gap: Memory Proxy wraps the wine process but cannot inspect what the Windows binary does inside its address space

normality_concerns.base_memory: 200-400MB overhead before the Windows app itself loads
normality_concerns.concern: Wine cannot run all Windows applications — driver-dependent software (DirectX 12, anticheat) will fail

darling.purpose: macOS API translation layer — enables execution of Mach-O binaries on Linux under JDesk Memory Proxy governance.
darling.status: Source present — CMake build required; GUI support experimental
darling.maturity: Less mature than Wine — CLI tools work reliably, GUI apps experimental

architecture.dyld: Dynamic linker — loads Mach-O binaries and their dylib dependencies
architecture.libSystem_B_dylib: macOS libc equivalent — wraps Linux syscalls
architecture.CoreFoundation: macOS base framework — strings, collections, run loops
architecture.AppKit_stubs: Partial GUI framework stubs — enough for some GUI apps
architecture.kernel_module: darling-mach.ko — Mach port IPC emulation in Linux kernel

threading_model.model: macOS GCD (Grand Central Dispatch) implemented via libdispatch on top of pthreads

concerns.THR_DARL_001: Mach port IPC emulated via darling-mach.ko — message passing between Mach threads goes through kernel module
concerns.THR_DARL_002: macOS run loops (CFRunLoop) implemented in userspace — correct nesting required for GUI apps
concerns.THR_DARL_003: Objective-C runtime (libobjc) thread safety — +initialize is not reentrant

security_concerns.SEC_DARL_001: Darling does NOT sandbox the macOS application — same Linux filesystem exposure as Wine
security_concerns.SEC_DARL_002: darling-mach.ko runs in kernel space — a vulnerability in it is a kernel-level privilege escalation
security_concerns.SEC_DARL_003: macOS code signing not enforced by Darling — unsigned Mach-O runs freely
security_concerns.SEC_DARL_004: SIP (System Integrity Protection) not emulated — macOS apps that rely on SIP restrictions will behave differently
security_concerns.known_gap: Darling is under active development — security model not audited for production use

normality_concerns.concern: Any macOS app that calls IOKit, Core Audio, or Metal will fail — these are not yet implemented in Darling

chromium.purpose: Full Chromium browser source — used headlessly by Dave (AI inference) and as a native desktop browser under JDesk.
chromium.status: Source present — requires depot_tools + ninja build (hours)

headless_usage.consumer: Dave (AI system) — headless Chromium for web scraping and inference context

threading_model.model: Multi-process architecture: Browser process + one Renderer process per tab + GPU process + Network service process
threading_model.browser_process: UI thread + IO thread + file thread
threading_model.renderer_process: Main thread (Blink) + compositor thread + worker threads (Web Workers)

concerns.THR_CHR_001: Each tab is a separate process — 10 open tabs = 10+ renderer processes = significant memory pressure
concerns.THR_CHR_002: GPU process crash causes all renderers to repaint — visible freeze
concerns.THR_CHR_003: --no-sandbox disables renderer process sandbox — a renderer exploit has full user-level access

security_concerns.SEC_CHR_001: --no-sandbox is required under JDesk (unprivileged user namespace restriction) — significantly reduces security
security_concerns.SEC_CHR_002: Remote debugging port 9222 must only bind localhost — never 0.0.0.0
security_concerns.SEC_CHR_003: Chromium auto-update disabled in source builds — security patches must be manually applied
security_concerns.SEC_CHR_004: PDF viewer (PDFium) is an attack surface — PDFs from untrusted sources should open in isolated profile
security_concerns.SEC_CHR_005: Extensions disabled by default in source build — if enabled, must vet extension manifest permissions

normality_concerns.memory_per_tab: 50-200MB per renderer process depending on page complexity
normality_concerns.concern: 5.5GB source tree — incremental builds require depot_tools and significant disk/CPU

drm.purpose: Deferred DRM (Digital Rights Management) userspace module with filesystem-level access control integration.
drm.status: Source present — Makefile builds drm.o and drm_kernel.o
drm.threading_model: Single-threaded enforcement at open/read/write intercept points
drm.integration: Hooks into VFS layer — integrates with negamane (immutability) and eperm (permission classes)

security_concerns.SEC_DRM_001: DRM enforcement must happen before data is decrypted and placed in page cache — enforce at VFS open() hook
security_concerns.SEC_DRM_002: drm_kernel.c runs in kernel space — buffer overflow in DRM parsing is a kernel exploit
security_concerns.SEC_DRM_003: DRM keys must not persist in kernel memory after session — explicit zeroing required
security_concerns.SEC_DRM_004: Feature branch origin/feature/add-drm-deferred-remove — deferred remove path must not leave dangling references

normality_concerns.check_latency: < 1ms per file open for DRM validation
normality_concerns.concern: DRM in the VFS hot path adds latency to all file opens — profile before enabling on high-throughput paths

wallpapers.purpose: Desktop wallpaper assets for JDesk and Galactic Cherry installer.

userland_set.count: 10 SVGs (Galactic Cherry theme: aurora-cherry, cherry-blossom-night, cherry-dawn, cherry-light, cherry-nebula, galaxy-core, galactic-cherry-default, minimal-dark, moonlit-ocean) + 10 JPEG renders

root_set.format: JPEG + BMP + SVG — Jessica Jones themed (14 scenes)

wallpapers.jdesk_usage: JDesk loads wallpaper from /opt/jdesk/wallpapers/ at startup — SVG preferred, JPEG fallback

normality_concerns.concern: BMP wallpapers are 24MB each — loading 14 into memory simultaneously would consume 336MB. Load one at a time.

threading_architecture.model: Multi-process userland. Each component is a separate process or JVM. No shared memory between JDesk/NWE/Chromium by default.

process_map.jdesk_jvm: JDesk JavaFX process — PID managed by systemd or xinitrc
process_map.nwe_jvm: NitroWebExpress JVM — managed by systemd nwe.service
process_map.chromium_browser: Multi-process Chromium — browser process + N renderer processes
process_map.chromium_dave: Headless Chromium — single renderer, remote debug on :9222
process_map.tomcat: Embedded in NWE JVM — not a separate process
process_map.xserver: Xorg — single process, multi-client via sockets

inter_process_communication.jdesk_to_native_apps: ProcessBuilder — launch and monitor only, no ongoing IPC
inter_process_communication.nwe_to_apache: AJP connector (port 8009) or HTTP reverse proxy
inter_process_communication.chromium_internal: Mojo IPC (Chrome's internal IPC — shared memory + message pipes)
inter_process_communication.jdesk_to_nwe: HTTP REST or telnet TUI (port 23) — no direct IPC

synchronization_primitives_used.javafx_level: Platform.runLater() for cross-thread scene graph updates
synchronization_primitives_used.x11_level: XLockDisplay/XUnlockDisplay when multiple threads use same Display*

intra_jvm_nwe.module_api: Direct Java method calls — modules implement NWE module interface
intra_jvm_nwe.event_bus: NWE internal event bus (custom) for module-to-module notifications
intra_jvm_nwe.database_bus: MySQL jvm_operand — shared state for multi-JVM observer circuit

intra_jvm_jdesk.javafx_events: Node event system — mouse, key, action events bubble up scene graph
intra_jvm_jdesk.process_monitor: Daemon thread per launched app — communicates exit code back via shared AtomicReference
intra_jvm_jdesk.native_callbacks: JNI callbacks from libjdesk.so — dispatched to Platform.runLater() queue

cross_process.nwe_to_client: HTTP/HTTPS responses, WebSocket frames, telnet line protocol
cross_process.dave_protocol: Chrome DevTools Protocol (CDP) — JSON-RPC over WebSocket
cross_process.kernel_to_user: Standard Linux mechanisms: /proc, signals, netlink, uevent (via udev)

process_isolation.ISO_001: JDesk JVM and NWE JVM are separate processes — a crash in one does not take down the other
process_isolation.ISO_002: Wine and Darling apps run as separate processes — Memory Proxy can kill them without affecting JDesk
process_isolation.ISO_003: Chromium renderer processes are isolated from browser process via seccomp (when sandbox enabled)
process_isolation.ISO_004: MySQL runs as mysql user — NWE connects as least-privilege jvm user
process_isolation.ISO_005: X11 display isolation — JDesk runs on :0; any other X clients on same display can capture screen/keys (see SEC_X11_002/003)

privilege_boundaries.PRV_001: JDesk runs as user mearvk — no root privileges required at runtime
privilege_boundaries.PRV_002: jdesk-provision runs as mearvk with sudo for apt-get only — sudo configuration must be scoped
privilege_boundaries.PRV_003: kali-provision installs pentest tools — must not grant those tools SUID/SGID bits
privilege_boundaries.PRV_004: wineserver socket — accessible only to mearvk (mode 700 /tmp/.wine-1000/)
privilege_boundaries.PRV_005: darling-mach.ko — loaded by root at boot; exposes /dev/mach to the mearvk user only

data_flow_validation.DFV_001: .jdesk-app manifest binary path — must be validated against allowlist before exec()
data_flow_validation.DFV_002: NWE HTTP input — all user-supplied parameters validated and sanitized before database queries (parameterized only)
data_flow_validation.DFV_003: Telnet TUI input — command parsing must handle NUL bytes, long lines, and control characters
data_flow_validation.DFV_004: jvm-config.xml — parsed at JVM startup with root permissions; XML injection must be prevented (DTD disabled)
data_flow_validation.DFV_005: Chromium --remote-debugging-port 9222 — must bind 127.0.0.1 only; SSRF from NWE could reach it

secrets_management.SEC_SM_001: MySQL password must not appear in jvm-config.xml or any committed file — use secrets injection at deploy time
secrets_management.SEC_SM_002: SSH private keys for observer circuit — stored in /etc/jdesk/ssh/, mode 600, owned root
secrets_management.SEC_SM_003: XAUTHORITY — mode 600, stored in /tmp/ with mktemp, not committed
secrets_management.SEC_SM_004: GitHub PAT — must be invalidated after use in CLI; never stored in git config
secrets_management.SEC_SM_005: Heap dumps at /var/log/jvm/ — may contain in-memory secrets; rotate and encrypt at rest

total_memory_budget.total_comfortable: 8GB RAM minimum for full stack with 2-3 open apps
total_memory_budget.concern: 16GB RAM recommended if running JDesk + NWE + Chromium + one Wine app simultaneously

disk_io_norms.jvm_heap_dump: Heap dump to /var/log/jvm/ can be 1-4GB — ensure disk space before enabling HeapDumpOnOutOfMemoryError
disk_io_norms.wine_prefix: ~500MB per WINEPREFIX after typical app install

process_count_norms.jdesk_running: 1 JVM + up to 6 native app processes
process_count_norms.chromium_running: 1 browser + 1-N renderer processes (one per tab) + 1 GPU + 1 network
process_count_norms.wine_running: 1 wineserver + 1 wine process per Windows app
process_count_norms.concern: Process count above 100 under normal usage suggests a runaway process or fork bomb

build_order.step_3: openjdk — extract boot-jdk-27, build openjdk-28 from source
build_order.step_5: jdesk java — compile JDeskApp + DesktopIconGrid + NativeAppLauncher with JavaFX 11
build_order.step_9: chromium — fetch chromium && autoninja -C out/Default chrome (hours)
